meta.note: Build map and source-based audit. Partial support is not a complete lesson or evidence of mastery. Years 7–9 allocation is proposed.
meta.scope: Year 1–9, GCSE Foundation/Higher, standard A-level pure/statistics/mechanics; Further Mathematics excluded.

edge_direction: Prerequisite -> dependent objective; activity/resource -> supported objective. Links are curriculum design, not mastery claims.

nodes.title: Count forwards and backwards to and across 100, starting at 0, 1 or another number.
Read and write numerals to 100 and number words from one to twenty.
Represent and compare numbers; identify one more or less using equal, more, less, most and least.
Count quantities and numerals in multiples of 2, 5 and 10.
Read, write and explain addition, subtraction and equality statements.
Use number bonds and related subtraction facts within 20; add and subtract numbers to 20, including zero.
Solve one-step addition and subtraction problems, including a missing number, using objects and pictures.
Solve supported one-step multiplication and division problems with objects, pictures and arrays.
Recognise, find and name a half as one of two equal parts of an object, shape or quantity.
Recognise, find and name a quarter as one of four equal parts of an object, shape or quantity.
Compare, describe, measure and begin recording length, height, mass, capacity, volume and duration.
Recognise coins and notes and their different values.
Order events chronologically and use language for dates, days, weeks, months and years.
Read and show o’clock and half-past times on an analogue clock.
Recognise and name common 2-D and 3-D shapes, including rectangles, squares, circles, triangles, cuboids, cubes, pyramids and spheres.
Describe position and movement, including whole, half, quarter and three-quarter turns.
Count in steps of 2, 3 and 5 from zero and in tens from any number, forwards and backwards.
Understand tens and ones; read and write numbers to at least 100 in digits and words, and represent or estimate them.
Order and compare numbers from 0 to 100 using <, > and =, and use place value and number facts in problems.
Recall addition and subtraction facts within 20, derive related facts to 100 and calculate mentally with two-digit numbers.
Use the commutativity of addition and its inverse relationship with subtraction to check and find missing numbers.
Solve addition and subtraction problems using concrete, pictorial, mental and written representations.
Recall and use 2, 5 and 10 multiplication and division facts; recognise odd and even numbers.
Write multiplication and division statements using ×, ÷ and =; know multiplication is commutative and division is not.
Solve multiplication and division problems using arrays, repeated addition, sharing, grouping and known facts.
Recognise, find, name and write one third, one quarter, two quarters and three quarters of lengths, shapes, sets and quantities.
Write simple fraction-of-quantity statements and recognise two quarters as equivalent to one half.
Choose standard units and tools to estimate, measure, compare and order length, mass, temperature and capacity.
Use £ and p correctly, combine money amounts and find different coin combinations with the same value.
Solve practical addition and subtraction money problems in the same unit, including change.
Tell, write and draw time to five minutes, including quarter past and quarter to.
Compare and sequence intervals, using 60 minutes in an hour and 24 hours in a day.
Describe and sort 2-D shapes by their properties, including sides and symmetry in a vertical line.
Describe and sort 3-D shapes by faces, edges and vertices; identify 2-D shapes on their surfaces.
Order and arrange mathematical objects in patterns and sequences.
Describe straight-line movement and clockwise or anticlockwise turns, connecting quarter, half and three-quarter turns to right angles.
Construct and interpret simple pictograms, tallies, block diagrams and tables.
Count, order, total and compare categories to ask and answer simple data questions.
Read, write and represent numbers to 1,000, understanding hundreds, tens and ones.
Count in multiples of 4, 8, 50 and 100 and find 10 or 100 more or less.
Estimate, compare and order numbers to 1,000 and solve practical place-value problems.
Add and subtract ones, tens or hundreds mentally from a three-digit number.
Add and subtract numbers with up to three digits using column methods.
Estimate and check with inverses; solve addition and subtraction problems, including missing numbers.
Recall and use the 3, 4 and 8 multiplication tables and corresponding division facts.
Write and calculate multiplication and division statements, including two-digit by one-digit multiplication, moving from mental to written methods.
Solve missing-number, positive-integer scaling and correspondence problems involving multiplication and division.
Count up and down in tenths and connect tenths to dividing a whole or a one-digit quantity by ten.
Use unit and non-unit fractions as numbers and find and write fractions of sets with small denominators.
Show equivalent fractions in diagrams and compare unit fractions or fractions with the same denominator.
Add and subtract fractions with the same denominator within one whole and solve related fraction problems.
Measure, compare, add and subtract lengths, masses and capacities using m/cm/mm, kg/g and l/ml.
Measure the perimeter of simple 2-D shapes.
Add and subtract money amounts to find change using pounds and pence in practical contexts.
Tell and write analogue time, including Roman I–XII and 12-/24-hour notation; estimate and read time to the nearest minute.
Use seconds per minute, days in months and ordinary or leap years; record and compare event durations.
Draw 2-D shapes, make 3-D models and recognise and describe solids in different orientations.
Recognise angles as corners and turns; identify right angles, multiples of a right-angle turn and angles smaller or larger than a right angle.
Identify horizontal, vertical, perpendicular and parallel lines.
Present and interpret data in bar charts, pictograms and tables with simple scales.
Solve one-step and two-step comparison questions from scaled charts, pictograms and tables.
Represent, estimate, order and compare numbers beyond 1,000, identifying all four-digit place values.
Count in multiples of 6, 7, 9, 25 and 1,000 and find 1,000 more or less.
Count backwards through zero into negative numbers.
Round whole numbers to the nearest 10, 100 or 1,000 and apply this to number problems.
Read Roman numerals to 100 and discuss the historical introduction of zero and place-value notation.
Use column addition and subtraction for up to four digits where appropriate; estimate and check using inverses.
Solve two-step addition and subtraction problems, explaining the operations and methods chosen.
Recall and use multiplication and division facts for every table up to 12 × 12.
Use place value, factor pairs and commutativity for mental multiplication and division, including ×0, ×1, ÷1 and products of three numbers.
Multiply two- and three-digit numbers by one digit using a formal written layout.
Solve multiplication-and-addition problems using distributivity, integer scaling and systematic correspondence.
Recognise and draw families of equivalent fractions.
Calculate fractions of quantities and use fractions to divide quantities, including non-unit fractions with whole-number results.
Add and subtract fractions with a common denominator.
Count in hundredths and connect division into tenths and hundredths to decimal notation, including 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4.
Divide a one- or two-digit number by 10 or 100 and explain ones, tenths and hundredths in the result.
Compare numbers with equal decimal places up to two places, round one-decimal numbers to whole numbers and solve simple fraction/decimal measure and money problems.
Convert between different measurement units and estimate, compare and calculate measures, including pounds and pence.
Measure and calculate rectilinear perimeters, including squares, in centimetres and metres.
Find areas of rectilinear shapes by counting squares.
Read, write and convert time between analogue, digital 12-hour and digital 24-hour clocks.
Solve time-conversion problems involving hours/minutes, minutes/seconds, years/months and weeks/days.
Compare and classify shapes, including triangles and quadrilaterals, using properties and sizes.
Identify acute and obtuse angles and compare or order angles up to two right angles.
Identify symmetry lines in differently oriented shapes and complete a figure across a given line.
Read and plot first-quadrant coordinates and draw sides to complete a specified polygon.
Describe translations as a specified number of units left/right and up/down.
Choose and use suitable representations for discrete and continuous data, including bar charts and time graphs.
Solve comparison, total and difference problems from charts, pictograms, tables and other graphs.
Read, write, order and compare numbers to at least 1,000,000 and explain each digit’s value.
Count forwards and backwards by powers of ten from any given number up to 1,000,000.
Interpret negative whole numbers in context and count in both directions through zero.
Round numbers to 1,000,000 to the nearest 10, 100, 1,000, 10,000 or 100,000 and use rounding in problems.
Read Roman numerals to 1,000, including years.
Add and subtract whole numbers with more than four digits using formal column methods.
Calculate mentally with larger numbers; use rounding to check answers and choose an appropriate accuracy.
Solve multi-step addition and subtraction problems and justify the chosen operations and methods.
Find multiples, all factor pairs and common factors; use prime, prime factor and composite vocabulary, test primes to 100 and recall primes to 19.
Multiply numbers up to four digits by one or two digits using formal methods, including long multiplication.
Use known facts for mental multiplication/division and divide up to four digits by one digit using short division with contextual remainders.
Multiply and divide whole numbers and decimals by 10, 100 and 1,000.
Recognise square and cube numbers and use squared and cubed notation in problems involving factors, multiples and powers.
Solve mixed-operation problems, interpret equality, and solve simple fractional scaling and rate problems.
Identify, name and write equivalent fractions, including tenths and hundredths; compare fractions with related denominators.
Convert between improper fractions and mixed numbers and record results greater than one as mixed numbers.
Add and subtract fractions whose denominators are equal or multiples of the same number.
Multiply proper fractions and mixed numbers by whole numbers with materials and diagrams.
Read and write decimals as fractions; understand thousandths in relation to tenths, hundredths and decimal equivalents.
Read, write, order and compare decimals to three places, round two-place decimals to a whole or one place, and solve decimal problems.
Understand percentages as parts per hundred and connect % notation to fractions and decimals; use familiar equivalents in problems.
Convert metric units and use approximate equivalences between metric and common imperial units, including inches, pounds and pints.
Measure and calculate composite rectilinear perimeters; calculate rectangle areas in cm²/m² and estimate irregular areas.
Estimate volume using unit cubes and estimate capacity with practical containers.
Convert units of time and solve measure problems using all four operations, decimal notation and scaling.
Identify 3-D shapes, including cubes and other cuboids, from 2-D representations.
Estimate, compare, draw and measure acute, obtuse and reflex angles in degrees.
Use 360° around a point, 180° on a straight line and other multiples of 90° to find missing angles.
Use rectangle properties to deduce missing lengths and angles; distinguish regular from irregular polygons by sides and angles.
Describe and represent a shape after reflection or translation and explain that its size and shape are preserved.
Answer comparison, sum and difference questions using line graphs.
Complete, read and interpret tables, including timetables.
Read, write, order and compare numbers to 10,000,000, explaining each digit’s value.
Round whole numbers to a required accuracy and solve practical place-value problems.
Use negative numbers in contexts and calculate intervals across zero.
Multiply a number of up to four digits by a two-digit whole number using long multiplication.
Divide numbers up to four digits by two digits using long division and short division where appropriate, interpreting remainders in context.
Calculate mentally with large numbers and mixed operations; apply the correct order of the four operations.
Identify common factors, common multiples and prime numbers.
Solve multi-step four-operation problems, including addition/subtraction contexts, and use estimation to check accuracy and reasonableness.
Use common factors to simplify fractions and common multiples for common denominators; compare and order fractions including those greater than one.
Add and subtract fractions with different denominators and mixed numbers using equivalence.
Multiply simple pairs of proper fractions and simplify the answer.
Divide proper fractions by whole numbers.
Connect a fraction with division and calculate decimal equivalents; recall and use common fraction, decimal and percentage equivalents in varied contexts.
Explain digit values to three decimal places; multiply/divide by 10, 100 and 1,000, and multiply one-digit numbers with up to two decimal places by whole numbers.
Use written division when answers have up to two decimal places and solve problems requiring specified rounding.
Solve relative-size and unequal-sharing/grouping problems using integer multiplication, division, fractions and multiples.
Calculate percentages of quantities and use percentages to compare situations.
Solve similar-shape problems when a scale factor is given or must be found.
Use simple formulae and express missing-number relationships algebraically.
Generate and describe linear number sequences.
Find number pairs satisfying an equation with two unknowns and enumerate possibilities involving two variables.
Read, write, calculate and convert standard units of length, mass, volume and time in both directions, using decimals to three places; convert miles and kilometres.
Investigate how shapes can share an area but have different perimeters, or share a perimeter but have different areas.
Recognise when area formulae apply and calculate areas of triangles and parallelograms.
Use suitable volume formulae to calculate, estimate and compare cubes and cuboids in cm³, m³ and other cubic units.
Draw 2-D shapes accurately from specified lengths and angles.
Recognise, describe and build simple 3-D shapes, including constructing nets.
Classify shapes and find unknown angles in triangles, quadrilaterals and regular polygons; use angles at a point, on a line and vertically opposite.
Name and illustrate radius, diameter and circumference, and use diameter = twice radius.
Read and describe positions across all four coordinate quadrants.
Draw and translate simple coordinate shapes and reflect them in the coordinate axes.
Construct and interpret pie charts and line graphs and solve related problems.
Calculate and interpret the arithmetic mean.
